premise: At 55, after 27 years as a court reporter, I loaned my stepson $128,000 from my pension to open a custom fountain-pen and archival-ink boutique, with a signed promissory note and 45% profit share, but after a luxury stationery chain offered $580,000 for the ink formulas and inventory, he transferred the business to his girlfriend's LLC and mailed me a $4,100 'nib' check. I found the original promissory note and a hidden email showing the transfer was fraudulent, voided the sale, and now run 'Ink of Deceit Writing Instruments,' where he grinds nibs in a smock that says 'Bled My Pension' and every receipt prints his fraud-docket number.
